note.explanation: Matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving. The forces between these particles and the way they move help explain the properties of solids, liquids, gases and plasma.
examples: Solid: its particles vibrate about fixed positions, so it has a definite shape and volume.
Gas: its particles are far apart, so it has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
note.checkAnswer: A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape. Its molecules can slide over one another, so it takes the shape of its container.
note.simple: Think of particles as tiny moving pieces. In a solid they stay close to fixed places, in a liquid they slide past one another, and in a gas they are far apart and move freely.
note.checkQuestion: Why does a liquid have a definite volume but no definite shape?
note.title: How particles explain the states of matter
steps: Identify how the particles are arranged and move.
Relate their motion and spacing to the forces between them.
Use these features to explain whether the substance has a definite shape or volume.
note.answer: Matter consists of very small particles that are always in motion. Their spacing, motion and intermolecular forces explain the properties of its states.

options: They move freely from place to place.
They vibrate about fixed positions.
They are motionless.
They are very far apart.
mcqs.stem: According to the kinetic molecular theory, how do molecules in a solid move?
rationales: Solids do not have molecules moving freely from place to place.
Correct: solid molecules remain at fixed positions but vibrate about them.
Solid molecules are not motionless; they vibrate.
Particles far apart are characteristic of gases, not solids.

options: They have no intermolecular forces.
Their molecules are fixed in position.
Their molecules can slide over one another.
Their molecules are spread throughout the whole container.
mcqs.stem: Which feature of liquid molecules helps a liquid take the shape of its container?
rationales: The section says liquids have intermolecular forces, though these are too weak to hold molecules fixed.
Fixed positions are characteristic of molecules in a solid.
Correct: liquid molecules can slide over one another in random directions, allowing the liquid to flow.
Particles spread throughout a container describe a gas.

options: It has a definite shape and volume.
It has a definite volume but no definite shape.
It has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
It has a definite shape but no definite volume.
mcqs.stem: Which statement describes a gas according to the particle model in this section?
rationales: A gas does not have a definite shape or volume.
This describes a liquid.
Correct: gas molecules are far apart, so a gas has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
This is not a property of a gas in the section.

options: Intermolecular force increases as distance increases.
Intermolecular force decreases as distance increases.
Intermolecular force is always zero.
Intermolecular force does not depend on distance.
mcqs.stem: What happens to intermolecular force when the distance between molecules increases?
rationales: This reverses the relationship stated in the section.
Correct: intermolecular force decreases with increasing distance between molecules.
The section describes a mutual force of attraction, not a force that is always zero.
The section states that intermolecular force depends on distance.

options: The average kinetic energy of its molecules increases.
Its molecules stop moving.
Its molecules' potential energy becomes zero.
Its molecules become fixed in place.
mcqs.stem: According to the section, what happens to a substance's molecular motion when it is heated?
rationales: Correct: heating makes molecular motion more vigorous, increasing the molecules' kinetic energy.
Heating does not stop molecular motion.
The section does not say that heating makes potential energy zero.
Heating does not make all molecules fixed in place.

options: A gas in which most atoms are ionized, containing positive ions and electrons.
A solid made only of neutral atoms.
A liquid in which molecules are fixed in position.
A gas whose particles cannot conduct electricity.
rationales: Correct: the section describes plasma as a gas with most atoms ionized and containing positive ions and electrons.
Plasma is not described as a solid made only of neutral atoms.
This does not describe plasma or a liquid.
Plasma conducts electricity because it contains positive ions and free electrons.

options: A liquid takes the shape of its container.
A solid has a definite volume.
A gas has no definite volume.
Plasma allows electric current to pass through it.
mcqs.stem: Which property is specifically linked to the presence of positive ions and free electrons in plasma?
rationales: This happens because liquid molecules flow; it is not specifically due to ions and electrons.
A solid's definite volume is explained by its closely bound molecules.
A gas's lack of definite volume is explained by its widely spaced molecules.
Correct: positive ions and free electrons make plasma a conducting state of matter.

written.text: Why solids have a fixed volume and shape according to particle theory of matter?
written.finalAnswer: Strong intermolecular forces hold solid molecules at fixed positions; they only vibrate about those positions, giving a solid a definite shape and volume.

rubric.why: The explanation must identify why solid molecules stay in place.
rubric.description: State that strong intermolecular forces hold the molecules at fixed positions.

rubric.why: The particle arrangement must be connected to the solid's properties.
rubric.description: Give the correct final explanation of the solid's definite shape and volume.
rubric.how: Mention vibration about fixed positions and state that the solid has a definite shape and volume.

modelAnswer: The intermolecular forces in a solid are so strong that they hold the molecules at fixed positions.
The molecules vibrate about their fixed positions, so a solid has a definite shape and a definite volume.

written.text: What are the reasons that gases have neither a fixed volume nor a fixed shape?
written.finalAnswer: Gas molecules are relatively far apart and can move freely, so a gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

modelAnswer: Gas molecules are relatively far away from one another.
They move freely, so a gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

written.text: Compare the spacing of molecules in the solid, liquid and gaseous state.
written.finalAnswer: Solid molecules are very close together; liquid molecules are close together but can move past one another; gas molecules are relatively far apart.

rubric.why: The comparison should include the close spacing in a solid.
rubric.description: Describe the spacing of molecules in a solid and liquid.
rubric.how: State that solid molecules are close together and describe liquid molecules as close enough to slide past one another.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish the widely spaced gas molecules from the closer particles in solids and liquids.

rubric.how: State that gas molecules are relatively far apart.

modelAnswer: In a solid, the molecules are packed closely together.
In a liquid, the molecules are close together but can slide over one another.
In a gas, the molecules are relatively far apart.

written.text: What is the effect of raising the temperature of a liquid?
written.finalAnswer: Its molecules move more vigorously and their kinetic energy increases.

rubric.why: The section relates higher temperature to more vigorous molecular motion.
rubric.description: State that the molecules move more vigorously.
rubric.how: Describe the increased motion of the molecules as the temperature rises.

rubric.how: State that the kinetic energy of the molecules increases.

modelAnswer: When a liquid is heated, its temperature rises and its molecular motion becomes more vigorous.
The kinetic energy of its molecules increases.

written.text: Is kinetic molecular theory of matter applicable to the plasma state of matter? Describe briefly.
written.finalAnswer: Yes. Plasma consists of freely moving positive ions and electrons, so its particles are in motion; plasma is a conducting fourth state of matter.

rubric.why: The answer should directly address whether the theory applies.
rubric.how: State clearly that kinetic molecular theory applies to plasma.

rubric.why: The particles present in plasma distinguish it from an ordinary gas.
rubric.description: Identify the ionized particles in plasma.

rubric.why: The theory describes matter in terms of particles that are in motion.
rubric.description: Describe the motion of the plasma particles.
rubric.how: State that the ions and electrons move freely.

rubric.why: This completes the description of plasma given in the section.
rubric.description: Give the correct final classification and property of plasma.
rubric.how: State that plasma conducts electricity and is called the fourth state of matter.

modelAnswer: Yes, kinetic molecular theory is applicable to plasma because plasma is made of particles that are in motion.
Plasma is a gas in which most atoms are ionized, containing positive ions and electrons.
These ions and electrons move freely in the volume of the gas.
Their presence makes plasma conducting, so it is known as the fourth state of matter.

written.text: Why would not you expect all the molecules in a gas to have the same speed?
written.finalAnswer: Gas molecules move randomly and have different motions, so they do not all have the same speed.

rubric.why: Random motion means the molecules do not all move in one identical way.

rubric.how: State that gas molecules move randomly.

rubric.why: The answer must give the conclusion about their speeds.
rubric.description: Give the correct final conclusion that gas molecules do not all have the same speed.

modelAnswer: Gas molecules move randomly.
Their motions differ, so they do not all have the same speed.

written.text: Describe the main points of particle theory of matter which differentiate solids, liquids and gases.
written.finalAnswer: Solid molecules are held at fixed positions by strong intermolecular forces and vibrate; liquid molecules can slide past one another; gas molecules are far apart. Thus solids have definite shape and volume, liquids have definite volume but no definite shape, and gases have neither.

rubric.why: The solid particle arrangement and motion are central features of the theory.
rubric.description: Describe solid molecules and their motion.
rubric.how: Include strong intermolecular forces, fixed positions and vibration.

rubric.why: Liquid molecules move in a way that distinguishes liquids from solids.
rubric.how: State that liquid molecules slide over one another or flow.

rubric.why: Gas particle spacing is a major difference from solids and liquids.
rubric.description: Describe the spacing of gas molecules.
rubric.how: State that gas molecules are relatively far apart.

rubric.why: The particle model should explain the observable properties of the states.
rubric.description: Give the shape and volume properties of solids and liquids.
rubric.how: State that solids have definite shape and volume, while liquids have definite volume but no definite shape.

rubric.why: This completes the comparison of the three states.
rubric.description: Give the correct final property of gases.
rubric.how: State that a gas has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.

modelAnswer: In solids, strong intermolecular forces hold the molecules at fixed positions, where they vibrate.
Therefore, a solid has a definite shape and a definite volume.
In liquids, the intermolecular force is too weak to hold the molecules at fixed positions; they slide over one another.
Therefore, a liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape and takes the shape of its container.
Gas molecules are relatively far apart, so a gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

explain.title: Particles are always moving
explain.body: According to this theory, matter is composed of very small particles called molecules which are always in motion. Their motion may be vibrational, rotational or linear. Molecules have kinetic energy due to their motion.

explain.title: Forces act between molecules
explain.body: There exists a mutual force of attraction between the molecules known as intermolecular force. This force depends upon the distance between the molecules. It decreases with increasing distance between them. Molecules also possess potential energy due to this force of attraction.

explain.title: Heating makes molecular motion more vigorous
explain.body: When a substance is heated, its temperature rises and its molecular motion becomes more vigorous which increases the kinetic energy of the molecules. Thus, the temperature of the substance depends upon the average kinetic energy of its molecules.

explain.title: Solids, liquids and gases
explain.body: In solids, strong intermolecular forces hold molecules at fixed positions, but the molecules vibrate about those positions. Liquids have weaker intermolecular forces, so molecules can slide over one another and the liquid flows. Gas molecules are relatively far away from one another, so a gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

explain.title: Plasma
explain.body: The plasma is a gas in which most of the atoms are ionized containing positive ions and electrons. These particles move freely. Their presence makes plasma a conducting state of matter, which is why plasma is known as the fourth state of matter.

mistakes: Do not say that molecules in a solid are motionless; they vibrate about fixed positions.
Do not say that a liquid has a definite shape. It has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container.
Do not say that a gas has a definite volume. It has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.
Do not say that intermolecular force increases as molecules get farther apart; it decreases with increasing distance.
Do not describe plasma as an ordinary gas: it contains positive ions and free electrons and conducts electricity.
